notes:
Summary: mid-market PLG SaaS (product analytics) evaluating Redwood. Started with Hosted API for fast iteration; now moving to a Dedicated POC to validate tail latency and cost at scale. Short notes / call fragments below.

Use-case + goals:
- Primary: in-app conversational support (support-agent) + contextual doc search for product docs and release notes. Secondary: reranking search results and periodic summarization for release notes.
- Traffic profile: steady 20–30 qps baseline, spikes to 50 qps for releases; typical request size small (100–400 tokens), some long context searches up to 2k.
- Latency target: p95 generation response < 400ms for short-turn chats; acceptable longer for large context. Cost sensitivity: strong (mid-market budget) — looking to trade quantization/batching for unit cost improvements.

Security / deployment constraints:
- Must run in customer VPC with private control plane for Dedicated (cannot rely solely on hosted for production).
- Require SSO/SAML, audit logs retention 1 year, KMS integration for key management, and EU data residency options for a subset of customers.

POC specifics (Dedicated):
- Duration: 2 weeks (prod-like traffic replay + synthetic spikes).
- Models: will test two variants — a quantized 13B variant for cost and a higher-quality 33B (float16) for quality baseline. Internal names: "vd-13q" (quantized) and "vd-33f" (baseline). Also want an on-hosted fallback model (hosted-redwood-small) for emergency failover.
- Canary plan: start with 5% traffic directed to Dedicated cluster (canary group), 95% stays on Hosted; after 24h of monitoring and automated regressions pass, increase to 20% then 50% then full switch if no issues. Canary monitoring metrics: latency p95, error rate, token-per-request cost delta, automated evals on a curated prompt set.
- Fallback & region failover: primary Dedicated cluster in us-east-1; fallback to hosted-redwood-small in us-east if Dedicated returns >1% 5xx or p95 latency breaches SLA for >10 minutes. Secondary region plan: if us-east suffers an AZ/region degradation, route to eu-west Dedicated replica with geo-aware routing; require cold-start latency tests during POC.
- Rollback criteria: automated eval quality drop >3% on prompt testset OR sustained SLA breach (p95 > 1.5x target for 10+ minutes) OR token-cost spike >40% vs baseline. Rollback to previous model variant or to hosted fallback.
- Observability asks: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency heatmaps, KV cache hit rates, failed-inference logs, and per-request trace IDs (for correlating with Fireflies transcripts).

Quotes / paraphrases from product lead:
- "We need predictable tails more than raw peak throughput — if you can't keep p95 low during release spikes we can't go live."
- "Budget needs to fit into ARR band; committed pricing vs burst is a must for us."

Open items / questions for Redwood team:
- Provide committed-capacity pricing with 6- and 12-month options and burst pricing model.
- Confirm VPC peering steps and expected lead time (their infra window mid-Feb).
- Share recommended quantization profiles and expected quality delta for vd-13q vs vd-33f (benchmarks + eval prompts).
- Confirm whether embeddings/fine-grained caching is supported in Dedicated with KMS-encrypted cache.

Next steps (short):
- AE: send POC SOW + committed pricing worksheet (Riley) — due 2025-01-20.
- SE: deploy canary config and run baseline replay tests (Maya) — start 2025-01-20.
- Legal: expect DPA redlines by 2025-01-27.
